errors.english: Although the third characteristic of the reason is indeed established as known
errors.why: The phrase completes ཚུལ་ from the previous side: 'the reason possessing the three characteristics (trairūpya)', not 'the third characteristic'.

fix.find: Although the third characteristic of the reason is indeed established as known
fix.replace: Although the reason possessing the three characteristics is indeed established as known

errors.english: positive concomitance means that everywhere the probandum exists, the presence of the reason pervades it
errors.why: Anvaya is that the presence of the probandum pervades the presence of the reason in every case; the English inverts pervader and pervaded.

fix.find: positive concomitance means that everywhere the probandum exists, the presence of the reason pervades it
fix.replace: positive concomitance means that in every case the presence of the probandum pervades the presence of the reason

note: Generally follows the argument on the need for 'ascertained' in the trairūpya, but misreads the opening term and reverses the direction of pervasion in the definition of anvaya.

errors.why: ལྡན་པ་ཅན་ is saṃyogin, the thing in conjunction; śaktimat means 'possessor of power'.

errors.english: it would not reside in both one line of text partially obscured or broken at the margin.
errors.why: The Tibetan simply continues 'not in both' onto the next side; the remark about an obscured line is invented.

fix.find: it would not reside in both one line of text partially obscured or broken at the margin.
fix.replace: it would not reside in both.

errors.english: and the certainty of arising from that are what follow
errors.why: It is the conveying power (gamakatva) that follows the ascertainment of tādātmya and tadutpatti, not the ascertainment that follows.

note: Follows the line of Karṇakagomin's argument on conjunction as a reason, but carries a wrong Sanskrit equivalent, an invented remark about the text, and a garbled conditional.

errors.english: Because it is accepted that the cause of attachment arises within the mental continuum, your example is invalid.
errors.why: Completing the previous side: the impassioned Yajñadatta is accepted as the very cause of the passion arising in Devadatta's continuum.

fix.find: Because it is accepted that the cause of attachment arises within the mental continuum, your example is invalid.
fix.replace: Because the impassioned Yajñadatta is accepted as the very cause of the passion arising in Devadatta's continuum, your example is invalid.

errors.english: However, this lacks a proven basis and therefore you have no valid example.
errors.why: The technical charge is that the example is devoid of the property to be proved (sādhya-vikala dṛṣṭānta), not that it 'lacks a proven basis'.

fix.find: However, this lacks a proven basis and therefore you have no valid example.
fix.replace: However, this example is devoid of the property to be proved, and therefore you have no example.

errors.english: so too the same logic applies here
errors.why: The Tibetan quotes the opponent's example and says it is empty of the probandum; there is no 'the same logic applies here'.
The speaker (ཁོ་བོ, the commentator) denies that Yajñadatta is the uncommon direct cause; it is not the opponent who refutes it.

In this discussion of passion and the impassioned (rāga/rakta) ཆགས་པ is the impassioned person Yajñadatta (who offers the flowers), not 'Yajñadatta's attachment'; the English conflates the two throughout.

errors.english: [note: referring to a technical point of Madhyamaka logic regarding self-causation]
errors.why: The passage concerns whether an example is sādhya-vikala in the rāga/rakta argument; the note about self-causation is misleading.

note: The dialectic over the example (dṛṣṭānta) is muddled: rakta and rāga are conflated, the sādhya-vikala charge is mistranslated, and the speaker is switched at a key point.

errors.english: just as with a cause of existence
errors.why: ཇི་ལྟར་སྲིད་པ is 'as far as possible / to whatever extent' (yathāsambhavam): to whatever extent there is a difference in the cause, there is a difference in the effect; it is not a 'cause of existence'.

note: A careful rendering of the argument on body, transformation and consciousness, with one misread adverbial phrase in the summary sentence.

errors.english: because it is logical that the essence of one distinct entity is separate from another distinct entity
errors.why: The Tibetan says it is NOT reasonable that the nature of one entity should be another, distinct entity.

fix.find: because it is logical that the essence of one distinct entity is separate from another distinct entity
fix.replace: because it is not reasonable that the essence of one entity should be another, distinct entity

errors.english: It is incorrect for space [note: original: (nam mkha'); space or ether] to possess a nature
errors.why: The subject, from the previous side, is the qualities such as pervasiveness: they cannot be the nature of space; it is not that space cannot have a nature.

errors.english: it is impossible for them to possess number, because those two [note: referring to number and collection]
errors.why: ལྡན་པ here is conjunction (saṃyoga); 'number and conjunction' are the two Vaiśeṣika qualities that are impossible, not 'possessing number'.

fix.find: it is impossible for them to possess number, because those two [note: referring to number and collection]
fix.replace: number and conjunction are also impossible for them, because those two [note: number and conjunction]

note: The regress argument against space having a distinct nature is mostly clear, but the opening reason is negated wrongly and the Vaiśeṣika quality 'conjunction' is misread.

errors.english: Why must we state that it is not solitary?
errors.why: It continues the opponent's challenge from the previous side: 'you must state why it is not solitary', a demand rather than a question about the need to say it.

note: Sound rendering of the momentariness argument and the variant reading; only the opening line of the opponent's challenge is misconstrued.
Faithful and terminologically precise rendering of the refutation of variegated conjunction (saṃyoga) and figurative designation.
Faithful word-by-word gloss commentary on the tigress episode; the only blemishes are garbled transliterations mixing Tibetan script and Wylie.
Faithful rendering of the sequence of the three kinds of faith and the teacher's instruction on stabilizing faith.

errors.english: established as valid cognition (pramana) reliable means of knowledge and its opposite, respectively
errors.why: The point is that waking and dream cognitions alike are pramāṇa or not by being non-deceptive or deceptive; 'respectively' assigns pramāṇa to waking and non-pramāṇa to dream, which the Tibetan does not say.

errors.english: is intended to be the producer of its own form
errors.why: མངོན་པར་སེམས་པ (abhimanyate) is the false conceiving or presuming of something as the producer of the cognition's form, not 'intending'; likewise its object is nothing but what is presumed, not 'what is intended'.

errors.english: [note: original: "skyes mos", referring to the Mimamsa school of Indian philosophy]
errors.why: Nothing in སྐྱེས་མོས་ (apparently a corrupt reading) identifies the Mīmāṃsakas; the note presents a guess as fact.

note: Follows the dream argument in outline, but the pramāṇa conclusion is skewed and the Yogācāra term for false conceiving is rendered as 'intended'.
